documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy: how it applies to generative AI
documents.summary: A short university page explaining how the Academic Integrity Policy applies to generative AI. Permission is left to each course and assignment, while users remain responsible for reviewing and owning AI-generated content.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule of its own; it quotes the Academic Integrity Policy that "the permitted use of AI may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment", so the decision goes to courses and assignments.

units.why: The quoted policy says "the permitted use of AI may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment", so whether AI is allowed is set per course and assignment. P04 fits; no tiers are named so not P05.
units.anchor: permitted use of AI may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment
units.frag_start: [t]he permitted use of AI may vary
units.frag_end: outcomes of the course or assignment.

units.why: The same sentence says variation is "based on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment", a distinct rule tying AI decisions to learning objectives, so P83 rather than P04.
units.anchor: based on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment
units.frag_start: [t]he permitted use of AI may vary
units.frag_end: outcomes of the course or assignment.
units.policy: AI permission is based on the specific learning outcomes of the course or assignment.

units.why: The subtitle says "the responsibility for the work stays with you", which makes students answerable for what they submit; P29 (own everything submitted).
units.anchor: the responsibility for the work stays with you
units.frag_start: what is permitted depends on your course

units.why: "Generative AI requires human input, editing and evaluation" followed by "It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy" tells users to check output; P31 chosen over P29 because the stated purpose is accuracy.
units.anchor: It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy
units.frag_start: It is our responsibility to review

units.why: This defines generative AI as tools that "generate new content based on existing data" and names Claude, Copilot and Gemini, setting what the page covers; P61.
units.anchor: These tools generate new content based on existing data from the internet or other databases

documents.unit: Center for Teaching and Learning Excellence / Academic Integrity Office
documents.title: Syllabus Requirements (required AI language statements)
documents.summary: The saved text of this Academic Integrity Office resources page is mainly navigation, advisor contacts and FAQs about reporting and student awareness of the integrity policy. It names no AI rule, only a "Required Syllabus Language" resource; the three AI statements described in the collect note are not in the saved text.
documents.stance_why: The saved page text does not reproduce the three required AI syllabus statements; it contains only academic-integrity FAQs and resource links, with no AI-specific rule. It sets no stance, so delegates.

units.why: The page links "Required Syllabus Language" and "Academic Integrity Syllabus Requirements" for faculty, indicating syllabus statements are required, though AI is not named here and the content is not in the saved text. Closest is P09, with a fit note.
units.anchor: Academic Integrity Syllabus Requirements
units.fit_note: Required syllabus language is listed as a resource but AI is not mentioned in the saved text.

units.why: "Students must open a summary of the University's Academic Integrity expectations in MySlice twice a year and provide their electronic signature" requires an acknowledgment of integrity rules; no type covers a signed acknowledgment, and AI is not named.
units.anchor: Students must open a summary of the University's Academic Integrity expectations in MySlice twice
units.frag_end: agreeing to uphold the AI policy.
units.policy: Students open a summary of the Academic Integrity expectations in MySlice twice a year and electronically sign to uphold the policy.
units.uncovered_note: Students must periodically read and electronically sign an acknowledgment of the academic integrity policy (AI not named).

units.why: "Most cases are reported by faculty and instructors via an online reporting system" describes the formal reporting route for integrity cases, so P81; it is not AI-specific in this text.
units.anchor: Most cases are reported by faculty and instructors via an online reporting system
units.fit_note: General integrity cases; AI is not named.

units.why: "Students and other University community members are encouraged to report possible violations" invites reports of violations; P71 is nearest although the passage is not about AI incidents specifically.
units.anchor: Students and other University community members are encouraged to report possible violations
units.fit_note: Reporting of integrity violations generally, not AI-specific incidents.

units.why: "informs them of their appeal rights" and consulting staff gives charged students a way to respond; P64 is nearest, but the passage is general integrity, not AI.
units.anchor: informs them of their appeal rights
units.fit_note: Appeal rights for any integrity charge, not AI-specific.

documents.title: AI for Students
documents.summary: An ITS hub for students that welcomes generative AI use, lists university-provided and approved tools, and suggests uses such as study schedules and brainstorming. It repeats that course permissions vary, and tells users to enter University data only into approved tools.
documents.stance_why: The page says "ITS is excited to help you incorporate generative AI into your day-to-day" and lists approved tools and uses, welcoming student AI use, while noting course rules vary under the Academic Integrity Policy.

units.why: The note quotes the Academic Integrity Policy that "the permitted use of AI may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment", delegating the decision; P04.
units.anchor: permitted use of AI may vary from course to course and assignment to assignment
units.frag_start: [t]he permitted use of AI may vary
units.frag_end: outcomes of the course or assignment.

units.why: "It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy" requires checking output; P31.
units.anchor: It is our responsibility to review and revise AI-generated content to ensure its accuracy
units.frag_start: It is our responsibility to review

units.why: "ITS is excited to help you incorporate generative AI into your day-to-day" welcomes student AI use, so P02 and encourage.
units.anchor: ITS is excited to help you incorporate generative AI into your day-to-day

units.why: "Claude Enterprise ... now available to Syracuse University faculty, staff, and students" is an institution-wide licensed tool, not one course, so P92 rather than P17.
